fields.meaning: How…, to what extent… (いかに)
examples: Being alone made me realize how important my family is.
No matter how hard you try, sometimes you don't get results.
This figure shows how serious the problem is.

fields.meaning: Whatever the case, either way… (いずれにしても)
fields.connection: いずれにしても + [sentence/clause] / いずれにしろ / いずれにせよ
examples: In any case, a conclusion will be reached tomorrow.
Whether you go or not, please decide soon either way.
At any rate, the responsibility is mine.

fields.meaning: Tinged with…, -ish, like… (with a negative nuance: 子供じみた)
examples: He made a childish excuse.
I don't want to hear any more preachy talk.
His theatrical attitude bothers me.

fields.meaning: …or not, whether… (か否か)
fields.connection: V (plain form) + か否か / N + である / Na + である / Aい
examples: Please let us know by the end of this week whether or not you will participate.
Whether that information is true or not is still unclear.
Opinions were divided over whether or not to carry out the plan.

fields.meaning: There is a possibility that… (可能性がある)
fields.connection: V (plain form) + 可能性がある / N + の
examples: There is a chance of rain from the afternoon.
There is also a possibility that this plan will fail.
Since it may have been an accident, the investigation will continue.

fields.meaning: …there is no end to it, endless (切りがない)
examples: If you start wanting things, there's no end to it.
If you worry about every little detail, there's no end to it.
There are so many problems that it would be endless to list examples.

fields.meaning: The most… of…, the best… in… (町きっての美人)
examples: He is the most outstanding employee in the company.
This is the most popular shop in town.
She is said to be the finest pianist in Japan.

fields.meaning: …beyond compare, extremely… (この上ない)
examples: It is the greatest joy to be able to meet you all.
An incredibly beautiful view spread out before us.
It is an utter nuisance.

fields.meaning: Partly because… (こともあって)
fields.connection: V (plain form) + こともあって / N + という / Na / Aい
examples: Partly because it was the weekend, the shop was crowded.
Partly because it rained, there were few customers.
Partly because it was my first time, I was very nervous.

fields.meaning: …like crazy, …nonstop (V+まくる)
examples: He has been playing games nonstop all day.
I bought clothes like crazy at the sale.
When I was asked questions at the interview, I ended up talking nonstop.

fields.meaning: Completely, (not) at all… (まるっきり)
examples: You can't trust a single thing he says.
I can't drink alcohol at all.
Even though they are twins, their personalities are completely different.

fields.meaning: Tinged with…, with a touch of… (春めく)
examples: The sunshine has started to feel like spring.
I can't forget his mysterious words.
Please stop speaking in that sarcastic way.

fields.meaning: It is thought that…, it is believed that… (ものと思われる)
fields.connection: V (plain form) + (もの)と思われる (もの)と見られる / N + (だ) / Na / Aい
examples: The culprit is thought to have broken in through the window.
The economy is expected to head toward recovery.
The cause of the fire is believed to have been a lit cigarette.

fields.meaning: Or… (written language: もしくは)
examples: Please apply by phone or email.
Fill in the form with a black or blue pen.
The person in question or their representative must come in person.

fields.meaning: It is not impossible that…, there's no saying that… won't (ないとも限らない)
examples: There's no saying an earthquake won't happen, so let's be prepared.
It is not impossible that it will fail, so I'll think of another plan as well.
There's no guarantee we won't be burgled.

fields.meaning: After all…, in any case… (何しろ)
examples: It's just so hot that I don't feel like doing anything.
After all, it's my first time, so I'm nervous.
There were just so many people that we couldn't move forward.

fields.meaning: …in one's own way (私なりに)
examples: I believe I did my very best in my own way.
Children have their own way of thinking.
The place is small, but we make the most of it in our own way.

fields.meaning: Without… (なしに/なしで)
examples: He took the day off work without notice.
You must not enter here without permission.
I can't read the newspaper without my glasses.

fields.meaning: Worth…, deserving of… (に値する)
examples: His efforts deserve praise.
This work is worth reading.
That is a proposal worth considering.

fields.meaning: Even down to… (listing down to the smallest detail: に至るまで)
examples: Everything, from clothing down to hairstyles, is set out in detail.
Everything is provided, from the furniture down to the tableware.
My grandfather kept working right up until the day he died.

fields.meaning: Even after it has come to… (に至っても)
examples: Even at this stage, he is still lying.
Even when it came to bankruptcy, the president did not admit responsibility.
Even on the day of the match, the lineup had not been decided.

fields.meaning: As for…, when it comes to… (に至っては)
examples: I'm bad at math, and when it comes to physics, I don't understand it at all.
My older brother is quiet, but my younger brother doesn't say a single word.
As for my grandfather, he won't even try to touch a smartphone.

fields.meaning: In the hands of…, when up against… (にかかっては)
examples: In his hands, even the hardest problem looks easy.
With my mother, no excuse works.
In her hands, even old clothes are transformed into something stylish.

fields.meaning: Using… as an excuse, on the pretext of… (にかこつけて)
examples: He is using his business trip as an excuse to enjoy sightseeing.
I used illness as an excuse to miss the meeting.
Using one excuse or another, I would go to see her.

fields.meaning: Being absorbed in… (and neglecting other things: にかまけて)
examples: Wrapped up in work, I had forgotten about time with my family.
I've been so busy playing that I haven't done my homework.
I'm sorry for the late reply; I've been caught up in how busy I am.

fields.meaning: Related to…, associated with… (にまつわる)
examples: I heard a legend associated with this temple.
There are many problems related to money.
There is a sad story connected with that ring.

fields.meaning: In accordance with…, in conformity with… (rules: に則って)
examples: The penalty will be decided in accordance with the rules.
The ceremony was held in accordance with tradition.
Please proceed with the procedures in accordance with the law.

fields.meaning: Cannot bear to…, not have the heart to… (に忍びない)
examples: I can't bring myself to throw away things that hold memories.
I can't bear to see him so depressed.
I don't have the heart to get rid of things that can still be used.

fields.meaning: Worth…, sufficient to… (に足る/に足りる)
examples: He is a person worthy of trust.
We obtained results that were satisfactory enough.
That is not an issue worth discussing.

fields.meaning: In light of…, based on… (に照らして)
examples: We make a judgment in light of past cases.
In light of the law, that act is illegal.
Speaking from experience, this plan is difficult.

fields.meaning: …is unreasonable, it is hardly possible to… (には無理がある)
examples: It is unrealistic to finish everything in one day.
That explanation is far-fetched.
Running the shop with this number of people is too much to ask.

fields.meaning: …there should be a limit to… (にもほどがある)
examples: A joke can only go so far.
That's rude beyond belief.
There's a limit to how much you can rely on other people.

fields.meaning: There is no need to…, it is not worth… (には当たらない)
examples: Even if he wins the championship, it's nothing to be surprised about.
A mistake of that degree is not worth criticizing.
There's no need to thank me. I only did what was natural.

fields.meaning: …beyond words, incredibly… (のなんのって)
examples: That dish was so spicy, it brought tears to my eyes.
I was so shocked, I couldn't even make a sound.
I'm so sleepy that it's all I can do to keep my eyes open.

fields.meaning: With… approaching, on the eve of… (を控えて)
examples: With the exam coming up, he studies late into the night every evening.
With the wedding next week, I'm swamped with preparations.
With my departure tomorrow, I don't think I'll be able to sleep.

fields.meaning: Taking advantage of… (をいいことに)
examples: Taking advantage of their parents being away, the children are running wild.
He is taking advantage of her kindness and using her.
Taking advantage of the other person's silence, he said whatever he liked.

fields.meaning: Regardless of…, without regard for… (を顧みず)
examples: Disregarding the danger, he jumped into the river.
I have done nothing but work, neglecting my family.
The doctors continued treatment without regard even for their own safety.

fields.meaning: Combining the purpose of… (を兼ねて)
examples: I went shopping, which also served as a walk.
We held a welcome party for him that doubled as a New Year party.
I watch Japanese dramas, partly as study.

fields.meaning: Taking the opportunity of…, using… as a turning point (を機に)
fields.connection: V (plain form) + の + を機に / N
examples: I quit smoking when I got married.
I took the opportunity of moving house to get rid of everything I didn't need.
Getting sick prompted me to reconsider my lifestyle.

fields.meaning: No one/nothing else but… (をおいて～ない)
examples: There is no one but him who can play this role.
I can't imagine anyone other than her as the leader.
You are the only one I can rely on.
